matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before exploring any stick move, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy. This tells you which side must increase or decrease and guides the search for a viable transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the very start of solving a matchstick equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick without first computing the side values, resulting in a change that does not address the actual imbalance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Systematically enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved, considering all characters (numerals and operators). A complete list prevents overlooking the correct move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after computing the numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Considering only moves between operators and ignoring a possible numeral upgrade, thereby missing the solution.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, determine how the move changes the numeric value of the affected numeral(s) or operator(s) and check whether it can bridge the discrepancy. This filters out moves that cannot affect the equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that turns ‘=’ into ‘-’ but leaves the numeric values unchanged, so the equation remains false.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the ‘=’ sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of its sticks can turn it into a ‘-’ sign, or adding a stick can create another operator. This provides a source of sticks that can be relocated while keeping the operator valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick is needed and the equation contains an equals sign.
matchstick.example: Failing to consider that a stick can be taken from ‘=’ to upgrade a numeral, thus missing a valid solution.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A ‘+’ consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a ‘-’, and adding a vertical can create a ‘+’. This yields extra stick‑source or stick‑target possibilities when a plus sign appears.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a plus operator is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the ability to remove the vertical stick from ‘+’, thereby overlooking a potential move.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one character to another, ensure that after removal the source character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator, and after addition the target character also stays valid. This prevents creating illegal symbols.
matchstick.example: Taking a stick from a ‘V’ and leaving a single angled stick, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Source character must stay valid after stick removal
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, verify that the character you are taking it from can lose that stick and still represent a valid numeral or operator. This guarantees the source remains recognizable after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately before executing a stick move.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an ‘X’, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: X↔V intra‑character transformation
matchstick.principle: When an X (two crossing diagonals) or V (two angled sticks) appears, consider moving one diagonal or angled stick within the same character to transform it into the other, changing its value by 5. This can resolve a discrepancy without touching other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the numeric gap equals the value difference between X (10) and V (5).
matchstick.example: Not considering that a V can become an X by adding a diagonal stick, thereby missing a valid upgrade.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to ‘-’ turns ‘=’ into ‘-’ and ‘-’ into ‘=’). This can balance the equation without altering numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When both source and target operators can remain valid after the stick move.
matchstick.example: Swapping sticks between ‘=’ and ‘-’ but not checking the resulting numeric equality, leading to an incorrect equation.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the numeric discrepancy equals the value change achievable by upgrading a numeral (e.g., V→X adds 5), look for an operator that can lose a stick while staying valid (such as ‘=’ becoming ‘-’) and move that stick to the target numeral to perform the upgrade. This directly resolves the imbalance.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a specific amount and a numeral can be upgraded by that amount using a single stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from ‘=’ to a ‘V’ to turn it into ‘X’ without checking the effect on ‘=’, resulting in a numerically balanced equation but an overlooked change to the operator.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick without checking whether the remaining strokes still form a recognized numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After selecting a source character, verify that the character without the moved stick still matches a valid Roman numeral or allowed operator.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on syntactic validity of characters and forgets to recompute the arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the numeric values of both sides after each candidate move and accept only moves that make the equality true.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may accidentally delete an operator or numeral entirely.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that every original token (numeral, operator, equals sign) remains present in the final string, even if its shape changes.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing ‘=’ to ‘-’ or vice‑versa is treated as a purely visual tweak, without considering how it alters the arithmetic expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Whenever an operator is altered, recompute the expression to see how the sign change affects the numeric result.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs the original equation unchanged, either by misunderstanding the task or by failing to generate a move.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly enforce that exactly one stick is relocated: pick a source character, remove one of its sticks, and place it elsewhere.
